judgment.notes: N004's numerical-state estimate applies with the stated mean-zero f,w, Sobolev bound M, delta<=1 and 0<tau<=1. N005 is applied to mean-zero inputs and smooth paths f,F_n. N006 supplies the stage and product estimates at the given gamma, and its constant-input cubic bound at s=gamma and s=0 on [n*tau,t], whose length is <=tau<=1 and left endpoint is nonnegative. Unitarity transfers each spatial product estimate to S_t inputs. At the zero-length endpoint all integrals vanish. There are no E/M applications.

S001 uses the bilinear endpoint difference J(f,f)-J(w,w)=J(f-w,f)+J(w,f-w), giving the H^1 difference O(delta); N006 then gives the small H^a_gamma and L2 stage norms. In S002, the square derivative uses N006 on partial_x(S_t A0) and S_t A0, while the difference of squares uses the H^1 algebra estimate, yielding O(tau^gamma+delta). Time integration and N004 give Q_n,W_n=O(tau*q). S003's projected-product identity and split f=w+(f-w) give Dinv B(f,F_n)=O(q), hence the stated bounds on Dinv Y_n' and Dinv Y_n. S004's normal form has coefficients 1/3 and -1/6: symmetry of J identifies its integral with Cint(f,f,f). Trilinear telescoping gives the exact-data O(tau^gamma) term and three O(delta) terms. Thus C_n,Y_n=O(q); mean-zero comparison then gives both the X bound and the stronger O(tau*q) negative-Sobolev bound. All constants inherit only M,gamma dependence.

scope: Coverage is reviewer-reported; reading alone is not mathematical assessment.
